Donald Trump has escalated his attacks on Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, calling him a “jihadist” and accusing him of wanting to impose Sharia law in the United States.
Speaking at a rally in Michigan, Trump invoked the September 11 attacks and questioned El-Sayed’s loyalty to the country.
He also alleged links between the Michigan-born Muslim politician and the Muslim Brotherhood. Trump offered no evidence to substantiate these claims.
